summary: A home-maintenance task tracker. Each task has a description, area of the home, due date, and an Open or Completed status. Users can add, edit, and delete tasks, mark them complete, reopen them, filter to open tasks, and see a live count of open tasks. All data persists in this browser across refreshes.
implemented_features: Add a task with description, area of the home, due date, and default Open status, with validation of required fields
Edit an existing task's details and save changes
Delete a task from the collection
Complete an open task via a Complete transition that sets status to Completed
Reopen a completed task via a Reopen transition that sets status back to Open
Open-task filter that narrows the list to status equals Open
Derived Open-tasks count metric shown alongside the collection
Local persistence in localStorage with malformed-data recovery, surviving a browser refresh
assumptions: The idea specified an open/completed status but not the exact option wording; I used 'Open' and 'Completed' as the two status option values.

The idea did not enumerate home areas, so I provided a curated list of common areas (Interior, Exterior, Kitchen, Bathroom, Bedroom, Living Room, Garage, Basement, Yard, Plumbing, Electrical, HVAC, Roof) with 'Interior' as the default.

The requested derived value is the open-task count; I expressed it as the schema's count metric conditioned on status equals Open, which the engine renders alongside the list. No source change was needed.
Due date is required so every open task carries a meaningful target date; validation surfaces when it is omitted.
The Complete and Reopen actions are modeled as declarative transitions gated on the current status, so repeated actions are prevented by the engine's repeated-transition protection.
